rationale: First full review round, run against branch Variant-1-Project-Hub at 1f045ba64 (codemie-ui) and EPMCDME-14781_project-model-settings at 7476f850b (codemie backend) — the state after the acceptance-criteria implementation but before any review fix-up. Six parallel finder lenses (blind scan, removed-behavior audit, cross-file trace, reuse/simplification/efficiency, altitude/conventions on the UI diff; one combined-angle pass on the backend diff) produced ~24 deduplicated candidates. Four 1-vote verifiers (recall-biased) covering every candidate confirmed 22 and refuted 2 (a claimed stale-data race in projectModelSettingsStore.saveMemberOverrides — refuted, it re-fetches fresh server state; a claimed redundant per-category `reason` write in BulkBudgetOverrideModal — refuted, required for correct per-category submission against a shared input field). Per the ranking rule, correctness/security findings outrank cleanup findings when a cap forces a cut; ranked by severity, the 10 emitted below are the blocking set (2 security, 8 correctness) and 12 confirmed cleanup/duplication findings were reported separately as non-blocking.

business_review.criterion: Updated Project Details information architecture is provided
business_review.notes: Overview/Members/Models/Budgets/Integrations tabs, each gated to the viewer's actual permission; Budgets tab route no longer redirects away.

business_review.criterion: UX supports project-level model allow-list or deny-list management
business_review.notes: Models tab persists mode/models to PUT /v1/projects/{name}/model-settings.

business_review.criterion: Design supports restricting models for selected projects or clients
business_review.notes: Per-project restriction is implemented; the platform has no 'client' entity separate from project, so that half of the criterion is not addressed and needs product clarification.

business_review.criterion: Design supports hiding expensive models from selected projects
business_review.notes: hide_premium_models flag, backed by the platform's existing premium-model alias config; no longer a hardcoded label list.

business_review.criterion: Model restrictions represented wherever a model can be selected (chats, assistants, workflows)
business_review.notes: GET /v1/llm_models?project= filters the list; chat, assistant-form, and workflow-editor selectors resolve project and call it via useProjectLLMModels. (Blocking finding CR-002 below shows this endpoint itself was not yet access-checked at this round.)

business_review.criterion: UX supports enabling or disabling automatic model routing for a project
business_review.notes: auto_routing_enabled switch on the Models tab, with per-router availability shown.

business_review.criterion: Automatic routing respects project model-availability restrictions
business_review.notes: A Switchyard router is offered only when both its capable/efficient candidates are allowed; a LiteLLM auto-router only when the project restricts nothing, since its candidates aren't visible to CodeMie.

business_review.criterion: Project Overview is compact and easy to scan
business_review.notes: Existing card layout preserved; new indicators follow the same card pattern.

business_review.criterion: Project Overview represents users, spend/budgets, model usage/distribution, integrations, routing impact
business_review.notes: Added model-availability, 30-day model-usage, integrations-count, and routing-impact cards alongside the existing users/spend/budget cards; routing card is gated behind the routing-analytics feature flag.

business_review.criterion: Structure supports adding future project-level capabilities without a full redesign
business_review.notes: Each tab is one route id, one PROJECT_DETAILS_TABS entry, and one render branch; adding e.g. MCP follows the same three-point pattern.

business_review.criterion: Design unblocks model-related work first while remaining extensible for integrations, MCP, budgets
business_review.notes: Model work is fully implemented, but the MR (by explicit user direction, kept from the prior designer-approved redesign) also ships substantial budget/member-management work; there is no MCP section or placeholder yet.

standards_review.notes: All commits on both branches use the 'EPMCDME-14781: ...' prefix.
npx tsc --noEmit and eslint clean on every changed frontend file; ruff check/format clean on every changed backend file.
CR-001 and CR-002 below are concrete access-control gaps in the new endpoints.

findings.title: Model-settings GET leaks peer member_overrides to any project member
findings.problem: get_project_model_settings() gates only on Action.READ, which any regular project member (Role.SHARED_WITH) satisfies, and returns the full ProjectModelSettings including member_overrides verbatim.
findings.impact: A non-admin member calling this endpoint can see every other member's user_id, disabled_models, and default_model — an information disclosure of peer-level administrative restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Strip member_overrides from the response for callers who cannot manage the project (i.e. lack Action.WRITE).

findings.title: GET /v1/llm_models?project= has no membership check
findings.problem: get_llm_models() loads and applies an arbitrary caller-supplied project's model_settings with no project_access_check(), unlike assistant.py's create/update_assistant which check access before consulting the same service.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can pass a project name they do not belong to and learn its model policy (allow/deny list, hidden premium models, resolved default) from the response shape.
findings.recommendation: Call project_access_check(user, project) before loading settings, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase.

findings.title: resolve_runtime_model returns the unresolved value instead of the fallback
findings.problem: `effective = requested or llm_service.default_llm_model` computes the model to actually use, but the allowed-model branch returns `requested` (possibly None/empty) instead of `effective`.
findings.impact: When the caller passed no model, the fallback this function exists to provide is defeated: `None` propagates into agent construction instead of the resolved default.
findings.recommendation: Return `effective`, not `requested`, on the allowed-model path.

findings.title: Test still asserts the old tab-specific unavailable copy
findings.problem: The unavailable-tab placeholder text was generalized to "This section is not available for personal projects." but the test still asserts "Members are not available for personal projects."
findings.impact: Confirmed failing; breaks CI on this branch.
findings.recommendation: Update the assertion to the new copy.

findings.title: bulkResetBudgets resolves even when every reset failed
findings.problem: Switched to Promise.allSettled and never throws when all per-user requests fail — it only shows a toaster.error.
findings.impact: BulkResetBudgetsPopup awaits the call with no exception, so it clears selection and refreshes as if the reset succeeded, alongside a contradictory error toast.
findings.recommendation: Throw when nothing succeeded so the caller does not treat the batch as completed.

findings.title: Bulk model override can save a default that the same edit just disabled
findings.problem: buildUserOverride preserves a member's stale default_model verbatim during bulk edits even when the admin's bulk toggle just disabled that exact model for them.
findings.impact: The saved override can have default_model equal to a model also present in disabled_models for that user — an internally inconsistent state that nothing blocks saving.
findings.recommendation: Re-validate the carried-forward default against the newly computed disabled set before saving; fall back to null (project default) if it's now disabled.

findings.title: Budget override errors collapse to one generic toast
findings.problem: handleOverrideMember calls store methods with silent=true and replaces any thrown error with a hardcoded generic message.
findings.impact: The backend's specific rejection reason (e.g. allocation exceeds available budget, 409 conflict) is discarded, leaving the admin no indication which category failed or why.
findings.recommendation: Surface the caught error's own message (parsedError.message / message) instead of a hardcoded string.

findings.title: Budget allocations cell can render blank
findings.problem: UserBudgetsCell dropped the guard that rendered an explicit placeholder when no category had allocation data; the new per-category filter can leave zero rows.
findings.impact: A member with no budget_assignments and no allocation lookup entry (e.g. a non-maintainer viewer, or a newly added member) sees an empty cell instead of a placeholder.
findings.recommendation: Render a placeholder when the filtered row list is empty.

findings.title: Undo control disappears after "Use project allocation"
findings.problem: hasCategoryAction is gated on allocationState === 'override' only, so once a category flips to 'pending-project' the action button (which the parent still wires as an undo handler for that state) is hidden.
findings.impact: After clicking "Use project allocation", the admin has no button-based way to undo the choice before saving.
findings.recommendation: Also show the action button for 'pending-project', with a label reflecting the undo action.

findings.title: "View details" override button is a no-op
findings.problem: OverridesSummary's "View details" button has an empty onClick handler.
findings.impact: Any category card with overrides shows a clickable control that does nothing, with no way to reach per-member override detail from that entry point.
findings.recommendation: Wire it to navigate to the Members tab (or a dedicated overrides view).
